root_cause_label: Naive GitHub API title-search without domain knowledge of authoritative paper code sources, compounded by failure to pivot after rate-limiting
one_sentence_failure_summary: The agent relied solely on generic GitHub API title searches to find official code repositories, lacking domain knowledge to use Papers With Code, arXiv, or known org repos as fallbacks, and after GitHub API rate limits blocked all remaining searches it repeated the same ineffective googlesearch strategy before prematurely declaring completion with 5 of 10 entries still empty.
t_err_evidence: Step 14: The agent commits to a GitHub API search function that uses only a naive name/description keyword match and returns the top starred result as a fallback, with no fallback to arXiv, Papers With Code, or parametric knowledge. Testing on paper 1 accidentally works, masking the fundamental weakness of the approach before it is applied to all 10 papers.
t_commit_evidence: Step 17: GitHub API returns 403 rate-limit errors for all 6 remaining papers. With GitHub API exhausted and the only alternative (googlesearch) already set up to replicate the same weak strategy, recovery is locked out given the agent's actual subsequent behavior.
t_surface_evidence: Step 15: Terminal output explicitly shows 'Found: None' for 6 of 10 papers, and result.jsonl is written with 6 empty official_code_url fields.
trigger_explanation: The agent lacked domain knowledge that research-paper official code lookup requires authoritative sources (Papers With Code API, arXiv PDF code links, known author/org repos) rather than a generic GitHub title search. A title-based GitHub API query with a star-rank heuristic is insufficient for papers whose repos have non-obvious names or are hosted under organization accounts with different slugs.
forewarning_evidence: Step 15 terminal output shows 'Found: None' for papers 2, 3, 5, 7, 9, and 10, directly signaling the search strategy is insufficient before any corrective action.
